newsitem.title: UK: Turkey wants economic compensation from U.S.
newsitem.headline: Turkey wants economic compensation from U.S.

text.p: Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller said on Friday she wanted compensation from the United States for losses incurred by her country's backing for the allied effort against Iraq.

"It's about time the United States proved they also stand by Turkey -- these losses have to be compensated," Ciller told BBC World television. "We only want a certain portion of our losses to be compensated economically."
Ciller said Turkey was working with U.S. officials on "the economic losses ... and how that can be compensated".

Turning to the security zone Turkey plans to create in northern Iraq, Ciller said it was a "must" for Turkey following the recent upheaval in northern Iraq. Turkey would "definitely" observe the territorial integrity of Iraq, she said.
"It (the buffer zone) is not taking advantage of anything and if it is seen as such it will be the worst mistake that anyone can make," Ciller said.
"It (the zone) means a fence strip right next to our borders has to be looked at as a security area which will deter penetration. It is going to be temporary kind of activity."
